definition: Shining or glowing in the night; used especially of the rare, ice-crystal clouds that form at extreme altitude and catch sunlight long after the sun has set below the horizon.
etymology: From Latin nox, noctis, meaning night, and lucere, to shine. The Romans used lucere for any kind of shining — lamplight, starlight, the gleam of a sword. English combined the two roots in the nineteenth century when scientists needed a word for clouds that had no business being bright after dark.
usage: On a November evening when the last color has drained from the west, noctilucent is the word for anything that keeps its faint, impossible glow — the frost on a fence post, a moth's wing, the thin cloud still lit miles above the sleeping world.
